not_authoritative_until: Prism reviews this proposed-contract.json, not only the request summary
Cap decides on Prism concerns with accept, reject-with-bounded-followup, or escalate
A contract-specific checker exists and accepts the authoritative contract
runtime/bin/redcap check includes or delegates that checker
forbidden_uses: treat this draft as a bypass for future Prism review

purpose: Govern 360-degree old RedCap archaeology by making every scan, extraction, migration decision, directory impact, and no-promote decision a bounded queue item before concrete module migration starts.

authority_inheritance.binding_rule: RedCap 1.0 verified and no_promote decisions are inherited by Phase 2 and cannot be reopened by queue placement alone.
authority_inheritance.reopen_rule: A 1.0 decision may be challenged only by a new bounded shard with exact sources, a new user directive or explicit Cap risk finding, Prism review, and a resolution that names which prior decision is being challenged.
authority_inheritance.non_override_rule: Phase 2 queue items may refine migration governance, but they may not override RedCap 1.0 exit criteria, terminal decisions, or no-promote records.

allowed_actors: Cap as main executor after RedCap gate
required_steps: Run runtime/bin/redcap gate for the amendment task
Name exact old source files before any old RedCap read
Provide one question, stop condition, acceptance criteria, risk level, expected output, and destination boundary hypothesis
Run Prism review for high-risk, structural, migration, deletion, hook, lifecycle, or directory-impacting amendments
Re-run runtime/bin/redcap phase2-blueprint check against the amended contract
Re-run runtime/bin/redcap check before treating the amendment as active
fresh_prism_required_when: the amendment adds a new old-source domain
the amendment changes classification taxonomy or destination boundaries
the amendment reopens a 1.0 verified or no_promote decision
the amendment changes hook, gate, lifecycle, or directory policy
forbidden_amendments: append a queue item with directory-only old sources
append a queue item without a stop condition
append a queue item that authorizes concrete module migration directly
use this contract as standing approval to bulk-read old RedCap

global_invariants.rule: Old RedCap access is exact-file-first; directory-wide bulk reads are invalid unless Norven explicitly authorizes a bounded exception.
A shard cannot advance only because it produced a report, review, receipt, ledger entry, closeout artifact, or summary.
global_invariants.enforcement_target: runtime checker plus final-claim guard integration

global_invariants.rule: Every extracted design idea must be classified as keep, redesign, discard, pathology, or no_promote before migration.

Every keep or redesign decision must name a destination boundary: runtime, runtime_prism, assets_contracts, assets_archaeology, assets_knowledge, assets_docs, host_adapter, or external_project_policy.
Every pathology or discard decision must state whether it needs a hard hook, deterministic gate, lifecycle rule, knowledge entry, no-promote decision, or no further action.
The current scaffold is a constraint, not a prison; any directory-structure change must be explicit, reviewed, and checked against the thin-root policy.
Provider disagreement is not hidden: Cap must record accept, reject-with-followup, or escalate for each concern/block before a shard advances.

definitions.keep: Portable old RedCap design can be copied or mirrored with small adaptation.
definitions.redesign: Design intent is valuable but old implementation shape is not portable.
definitions.discard: Neither design nor implementation should enter new RedCap.
definitions.pathology: Old design or workflow contributed to failure modes and needs an explicit guardrail decision.
definitions.no_promote: The lesson is retained, but the old module or mechanism is intentionally not promoted.

enforced_by_checker: private archive and raw prism run path patterns are rejected when disabled
when the old RedCap root is reachable, every exact source must be a readable file

phases.name: Inventory From Existing Source Maps
phases.entry_rule: Use assets/archaeology/shards/index.json and current no-promote/extraction records before opening any old RedCap file.
phases.exit_rule: Every candidate domain has an exact-source shard or an explicit blocked reason.

phases.name: Bounded Extraction
phases.entry_rule: One shard question, exact source list, stop condition, and acceptance criteria exist.
phases.exit_rule: Extraction records portable guarantees, discard/defer choices, read policy, and verification evidence.

phases.name: Classification And Governance
phases.entry_rule: Extraction exists or a no-promote record exists.
phases.exit_rule: Every design idea has a classification, destination boundary, hook/gate assessment, and verification route.

phases.name: Migration Review
phases.entry_rule: Only keep/redesign ideas with destination boundaries can enter migration review.
phases.exit_rule: Prism and lifecycle authorize concrete implementation or the item is blocked/escalated.

phases.name: Verified Migration
phases.entry_rule: Concrete implementation has a lifecycle packet and gate decision.
phases.exit_rule: Changed runtime/contract/knowledge reality is verified by item-specific checks and runtime/bin/redcap check.

initial_queue.question: Which old RedCap rules separate runtime root, project workspace, and user-private state?
initial_queue.stop_condition: Use the already extracted boundary shard; do not reopen old sources unless a later review names a missing question.
acceptance_criteria: Portable guarantees are mapped to runtime boundary implementation or explicit defer choices

initial_queue.question: Which old review tracks are portable without duplicating the new FSM?
initial_queue.stop_condition: Extract review-track semantics only; do not migrate old report bodies or create a second state machine.
acceptance_criteria: Useful lifecycle evidence maps to the current development_lifecycle validator
Any duplicate FSM behavior is classified redesign or no_promote

initial_queue.question: Which old long-task defenses should become Prism shard ledger rules?
initial_queue.stop_condition: Extract split, budget, context, and acceptance rules only; do not import old task ledgers wholesale.
acceptance_criteria: Long tasks split into bounded shard accounts
Cap-owned acceptance remains separate from provider output
Context-heavy artifacts are index-first rather than default-loaded

prior_decisions.binding_effect: Reports remain support evidence only and cannot satisfy completion alone.
prior_decisions.reopen_requires: new bounded evidence plus Prism concern resolution

prior_decisions.binding_effect: Receipts remain proof after changed reality and cannot become completion authority.
prior_decisions.reopen_requires: new bounded evidence plus Prism concern resolution

prior_decisions.binding_effect: Closeout evidence is support-only and old closeout runtime is not promoted by default.
prior_decisions.reopen_requires: new bounded evidence plus Prism concern resolution

prior_decisions.binding_effect: Raw evidence stays explicit-access and is not default context.
prior_decisions.reopen_requires: new bounded evidence plus Prism concern resolution

initial_idea_records.summary: Workspace-oriented commands must resolve the managed project workspace and task file from caller context instead of defaulting into RedCap runtime root.

Self-development may make project_workspace equal runtime_root, but only as an explicit exception; the old idea is valuable while the exception handling must be redesigned around the current boundary resolver and lifecycle gate.
Status and diagnose output should expose runtime root, project workspace, task file, and user-state policy.
Revive, summary, doctor, and debug-style commands should share the same workspace and task-file resolution instead of each command inventing a fallback.
Long-task work must load indexes first and treat raw or large artifacts as explicit references, never default context.
Long tasks should be split into Prism shard accounts with explicit source budgets, provider round limits, stop conditions, and output schemas.
Provider output and reports are support evidence only; Cap-owned acceptance remains separate and must be encoded in shard account policy.
Report or summary presence must never complete a task without runtime, contract, knowledge, or RedCap command evidence.

minimum_assertions: status is active only for authoritative contract path, never for evidence drafts
all queue entries contain exact_old_sources and no directory paths
all queue entries contain stop_condition and acceptance_criteria
all idea records use constrained classification and destination values
no entry with status verified depends only on docs, reports, ledgers, receipts, or reviews
runtime/bin/redcap check delegates or includes this checker

human_intervention_rules: Ask Norven before reading private archives, raw prism runs, old task bodies, old receipts, or old closeout ledgers.
Ask Norven before deleting, moving, or pruning old RedCap evidence.
Ask Norven before changing provider policy or adding providers beyond Kimi and Claude Code.
Ask Norven before changing Cap identity, soul loader semantics, or user-private state boundaries.
phase2_exit_criteria: The authoritative contract exists under assets/contracts.
The contract-specific checker exists and is included in runtime/bin/redcap check.
Every initial queue item is represented in the authoritative contract.
At least one item that is currently queued in the authoritative contract reaches verified through bounded extraction before Phase 2 can authorize concrete old module migration.
At least one keep/redesign idea and one pathology/no_promote prior decision pass checker validation.
Prism has reviewed the authoritative contract and any concerns have accepted/rejected/escalated resolutions.
No concrete old module migration has started before the contract is active.
